title: Variable and Assignment
definition: A variable is a named binding to program state, and assignment establishes or changes the value associated with that binding.
purpose: Make named program state and its transitions explicit and traceable.
history: Variables and assignment are central abstractions of imperative programming, separating names from the values associated with them over time.
mental_model: A binding table associates a name with a current value; each assignment creates an observable before-and-after state transition.
analogy: A labeled whiteboard field can be updated; the analogy fails because language bindings, values, scope, and object identity follow formal rules rather than physical boxes.
relationships: binds a name to a value
industry_notes: State transitions should be named, bounded, observable, and tested against invariants.
ai_notes: AI-generated assignments must be audited with a state table and invariant checks rather than accepted from a final output alone.
interview_notes: Ask the candidate to trace a sequence of assignments and distinguish declaration, initialization, assignment, and mutation.
exercise_candidates: Produce a complete state table for an account update sequence
lab_candidates: Trace account state and identify unnecessary mutation
project_candidates: Control state in a data transformation console
